text.headline: Timeline of Hungary
text.text: Major events in the history of Hungary.

events.headline: Foundation of the Hungarian State
events.text: The early Hungarians, known as the Magyars, began settling in the Carpathian Basin around this time, establishing the foundations of what would become the Hungarian state.

events.headline: Conquest of the Carpathian Basin
events.text: Led by Árpád, the Magyars conquered the Carpathian Basin, marking the beginning of Hungarian history as a unified entity.

events.headline: Stephen I Crowned King
events.text: Stephen I was crowned the first King of Hungary, establishing the Christian Kingdom of Hungary and promoting the spread of Christianity.

events.headline: Mongol Invasion
events.text: The Mongol invasion led to significant destruction in Hungary, resulting in the death of a large portion of the population and the eventual rebuilding of the country.

events.headline: End of the Árpád Dynasty
events.text: The death of Andrew III marked the end of the Árpád dynasty, leading to a power struggle and the eventual rise of the Anjou dynasty.

events.headline: Battle of Mohács
events.text: The Ottoman Empire defeated the Hungarian forces at the Battle of Mohács, leading to the partition of Hungary and significant Ottoman influence in the region.

events.headline: Buda Falls to the Ottomans
events.text: The city of Buda fell to the Ottomans, marking the beginning of over a century of Ottoman rule in parts of Hungary.

events.headline: Recapture of Buda
events.text: The Habsburgs, along with their allies, recaptured Buda from the Ottomans, marking the beginning of the end of Ottoman rule in Hungary.

events.headline: Hungarian Revolution of 1848
events.text: A nationwide revolution against Habsburg rule began, demanding independence and civil rights, leading to a brief period of self-governance.

events.headline: Austro-Hungarian Compromise
events.text: The Austro-Hungarian Compromise established the Dual Monarchy, granting Hungary significant autonomy within the Austro-Hungarian Empire.

events.headline: Start of World War I
events.text: Hungary, as part of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, entered World War I, which would lead to significant territorial losses and political changes.

events.headline: Treaty of Trianon
events.text: The Treaty of Trianon was signed, resulting in the loss of two-thirds of Hungary's territory and a significant reduction in population.

events.headline: Nazi Occupation
events.text: Nazi Germany occupied Hungary, leading to the deportation of hundreds of thousands of Jews and other minorities to concentration camps.

events.headline: Hungarian Revolution of 1956
events.text: A nationwide revolt against the Soviet-imposed policies erupted, leading to a brief period of freedom before Soviet forces crushed the uprising.

events.headline: Reburial of Imre Nagy
events.text: The reburial of Imre Nagy, a leader of the 1956 Revolution, symbolized the end of communist rule and the beginning of democratic reforms in Hungary.

events.headline: First Free Elections
events.text: Hungary held its first free elections after the fall of communism, marking a significant step towards democracy.

events.headline: Hungary Joins the EU
events.text: Hungary became a member of the European Union, marking a significant milestone in its integration into the European community.

events.headline: Fidesz Party Gains Power
events.text: The Fidesz party, led by Viktor Orbán, won a two-thirds majority in the parliamentary elections, leading to significant political changes and reforms.

events.headline: COVID-19 Pandemic
events.text: Hungary, like many countries, faced the challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to health crises and economic impacts.

events.headline: Russian Invasion of Ukraine
events.text: The Russian invasion of Ukraine had significant geopolitical implications for Hungary, affecting its energy policies and regional security.
